# Debug: inspect which placements are chosen for demo3. Also note comp 0/5 domino "1,1" vertical at (3,12),(4,12) — those 1s form their own small object, but also anchor candidates. Spurious extras like (2,2)=1 suggest stamping the domino or another shape.
# First: enumerate all candidate placements (consistent vs input) and see which map onto expected additions.
inp=G['Demo pair 3 input']; out=G['Demo pair 3 output']
h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0]); bg=6
cs=comps(inp)
singles=[next(iter(t)) for t in cs if len(t)==1]
templates=[sorted(t) for t in cs if len(t)>1]
added={(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if inp[r][c]==bg and out[r][c]!=bg}
print('singles',singles)
cands=[]
for T in templates:
    cols={p:inp[p[0]][p[1]] for p in T}
    for s in singles:
        ar,ac=s
        for (tr,tc) in T:
            if inp[tr][tc]!=inp[s[0]][s[1]]: continue
            off=(ar-tr,ac-tc)
            cells=[(r-off[0],c-off[1]) for r,c in T]
            if any(not(0<=r<h and 0<=c<w) for r,c in cells): continue
            if all(inp[r][c]==bg or inp[r][c]==cols[(r2,c2)] for (r,c),(r2,c2) in zip(cells,T)):
                cov=len({(r,c) for r,c in cells if inp[r][c]==bg} & added)
                cands.append((cov,len(T),tuple(cells)[:1],s,tuple(sorted(T))[:3]))
cands.sort(reverse=True)
print(cands[:6])

So motifs: {5,7} diagonal-ish pair separated by gaps; and 2/4 motif. Rule maybe: pairs of same color separated diagonally get... Let's look: added cells: 5@(12,2): relative to 5@(13,0)? offset (-1,+2). 7@(14,0): relative to 7@(13,2) offset (+1,-2). Hmm these form pattern around existing 5@(13,0),7@(13,2): like a plus/diamond completing? Actually (13,0)5 and (13,2)7 exist in INPUT already! Input row13: "5 0 7". Output adds 5@(12,2) and 7@(14,0). Input rows 19-22: "0 0 0 0 0 4 2 4 4 0 / 0 0 0 0 0 4 0 4 4 0 / 0 5 0 0 0 4 4 4 4 0 / 0 7 0 0 0 4 0 0 0 0". So input has vertical pair 5@(20,1) and 7@(21,1) too, and 5@(22,3),7? no.

Output additions for the 5/7 motif: around each single 5 and 7? Input singles with additions:
- 2@(4,7) → got 4x4 motif stamped above-right anchored by 2? In output copy rows 4-7 cols 6-9, with 2 at (4,7). Input motif's 2 at (18,6). Offset between anchor 2 positions: copy at (4,6)-(7,9), original at (18,5)-(21,8). Copy = original translated by (-14,+1)? Original rows18-21 cols5-8; output copy rows4-7 cols6-9. So translation (-14,+1). Hmm why this placement? Maybe because the isolated 2@(4,7)... no.

Alternative: rule = the motif stamps so that its own structure completes other partial structures. Consider "5/7" motif in input: vertical domino 5@(20,1),7@(21,1) exists, and scattered singles: 5@(13,0),7@(13,2),5@(22,3)?? wait (22,3)=0? input row 22: "0 0 0 5 0..." yes 5@(22,3). Output added: 5@(12,2), 7@(14,0), 7@(23,3)?? output row 23 col3=7. Hmm wait earlier diffs show only rows 4-7 and 12,14. But also (22,3)5 unchanged.

Wait actually maybe simpler: 5@ and 7 pairs: in output, each existing single 5 gets 7 added below-left? 5@(13,0): added 5@(12,2)? That's not adjacent.

Let me reconsider: maybe there are two shapes: shape A = the 4x4 block containing 2 and 4s, shape B = vertical domino 5/7. Stamp each shape at every position where the matching cell lands on an isolated pixel, direction such that partner goes into bg. For demo6: 
- 5@(13,0): stamp vertical domino 5@(r,c),7@(r+1,c) anchored at 5 with 7 going down. Then added would be 7@(14,0) ✓!! Yes out(14,0)=7 ✓.
- 7@(13,2): stamp 5 above: 5@(12,2) ✓ (out(12,2)=5). 
- For 2@(4,7): stamp the 4x4 motif anchored at its 2 cell. Placement: which orientation? Only one valid if all other cells must be bg. Anchor 2@(18,6), other cells: (18,5)=4? that's part of motif... anchor = 2 cell; others land on bg ✓. When stamping onto isolated 2@(4,7): place motif with 2 at (4,7): then 4s at (4,8),(4,9),(5,7),(5,8)? wait check original motif cells: (18,5)=4,(18,6)=2,(18,7)=4,(18,8)=4,(19,5)=4,(19,6)=4?? input row19: cols5,7,8 are 4, col6=0. Row 20: col5=4,cols6,7,8,9? row20: "0 5 0 0 0 4 4 4 4 0" -> cols 5,6,7,8=4. Row 21: col5=4.

So motif relative to 2@(18,6): 4 at (0,-1),(0,1),(0,2),(1,-1),(1,1),(1,2),(2,-1),(2,0),(2,1),(2,2),(3,-1),(3,1),(3,2),(3,3). Check against output copy at 2@(4,7): (4,6),(4,8),(4,9),(5,6),(5,8),(5,9),(6,6),(6,7),(6,8),(7,6),(7,8),(7,9). Output rows 4-7:
row4: cols 6=4,7=2,8=4,9=4 ✓

row7: col6=4 only ✓
Matches! Great.

So the rule: extract multi-cell connected components (multi-color? here motif has colors 4 and 2, both non-zero). For each component, for each colored cell within it, stamp the component translated so that cell maps onto any same-colored cell elsewhere in the grid, provided the rest of the component falls on background and in bounds. Verify on demo 5 & 3, 4.

Demo 5: motifs: (7,8)6-(7,9)4 horizontal, (7,8)6-(8,8)4 vertical, (8,0)2-(8,1)1 horizontal. Anchor each single of matching color. Valid placements must have other cells on bg. But I previously got extra stamps. Why extra? Because anchor could ALSO land on cells of existing multi-components... In demo5 some stamps overlapped other objects' cells (conflict with existing non-bg cells other than anchor). My constraint `all(I[pp][qq]==bg or ...)` allows anchor coinciding with... only anchor allowed to be non-bg besides bg. That should prevent overlaps. But mismatch had over-stamps like (0,10,4) etc. Wait those were my previous version's issues; let me just test now on all demos. Also demo6 stamps may overlap other stamps. In demo 6, stamp anchored at 2@(4,7) uses cells (4,6),(4,8),(4,9),(5,6),(5,8),(10? etc.) — none overlap anything else. Good.

Key remaining question: do stamps apply to isolated pixels AND cells belonging to other motifs? In demo6, stamp anchored at 2@(4, output doesn't show stamp near 9@(10,9),8@(9?)... 9 and 8 aren't in motif colors (2,4). Right.

The bug: in solve2 earlier I required anchors to be "isolated singles" (components of size 1), whereas valid placements could also anchor at other single cells not connected (i.e., cells not part of a multi-comp). Both fine. Demo5 mismatches were from diag shape ((8,8),(9,9)): in input there IS a diagonal adjacency (8,8)4 and (9,9)6 — different colors, so treated as motif. But expected output does NOT stamp from it. Hmm, so maybe not all adjacent pairs count — only orthogonal adjacency counts as motif! Demo6's 4x4 motif contains diagonal adjacencies too though. Use only orthogonal-adjacent pairs? But motif includes diagonal cells (e.g. (21,5)=4 and (21,6)=0...). Orthogonal adjacency suffices to define full components. Component extraction handles full object.

But demo5 issue with over-stamping arose because I used all four orientations of each shape via anchor-based stamping — e.g., rotations/reflections? No: shape ((8,8),(9, try rotation? e((8, relative offsets set {(0,0),(0,1)} for H and {(0, normalized) V} distinct components already capture all orientations.

Wait — validity condition in demo5 failed to produce 0 because I required BOTH anchor cell and other cells all on bg... In demo5 output, some stamps DO involve cells overlapping existing objects, e.g., a stamp anchored at (1,11)6 with 4 added at (1,12). Input has 6@(1,11); stamp 6-4H with 6 at anchor (1,11), 4 at (1,12): valid since (1,12) is bg. This should be caught by my code... unless my validation only allowed stamp placements where anchor cell equals a single... it allowed anchor to be ANY cell whose color matches.

Hmm, so demo5 extra stamps came from the diagonal shape ((8,8)4,(9,9) in input at (8,8),(9,9)). Expected output DOES add things related to this shape? In demo5 output, is there any addition associated with the 4@(8,8)-6@(9,9) diagonal pair? Looking at diff list earlier: additions near (7,11),(8,11),(9,12) etc. Added (7,11,6) next to 4@(7,12)? Earlier analysis showed added 6@(7,11) with anchor 4@(7,12)? Hmm wait there was a stamp: 6@(7,11) and 4@(8,11)? and added 4@(2,11)? These suggest multiple copies including diagonal variants. Expected output did include stampings from the diagonal motif ((8, used for additions (7,11)6,(8,11)? Let me check: expected output around (7,11): out row7 shows '64' at 11-12, out row8 col11=4, out row plus? Actually earlier analysis showed stamp with 6 at (7,11) and 4 at (canonical shape ((8,8)4,(9,6)).

Hmm, so the diagonal motif WAS used in demo5. So all 4 motifs were stamped. So demo5 over-stamps must come from something else — maybe the issue is ordering: stamping sequentially updates O while checking validity against ORIGINAL I? That's what I did (check against I). Over-stamps in mismatches like (0,10,4,8): predicted 4@(0,10)? Which anchor explains (0,10,4)? From shape ((8,8,4),(9,9,6)) diag, anchored at 4@(8,8)? off=(1,1), stamp 6@(2,... ) hmm (0,10)? no.

Actually the earlier mismatches at (0,10,4),(0,23,6),(1,0,6),(1,3,6)... might stem from treating the 2-1 motif wrongly. E.g., "2-1" motif horizontal "21": anchored at 2, 1 goes right. But 1-singles exist too — anchoring at 1 gives 2 to left. In output, do both happen? e.g. 2@(0,16)→1@(0,17) ✓; 1@(5,6)→2@(5,5) ✓. Consistent.

So demo5 issue likely the "all other cells bg" constraint + anchor-on-single requirement. The mismatch listed earlier had entries like (0,10,4,8): predicted 4@(0,10)? Which stamp gave that? Shape ((8,8,4),(9, 9,6)) anchored at 6@(9,9): offset for 4 = (-1,-1). Place anchor 6@(9,9)? but (9,9) is a single; stamp 4@(8,8). Input (8,8)=4 already non-bg... invalid under strict rule. Hmm (8,8) is itself a single. So maybe the real rule: stamp valid only when OTHER cells land on bg OR on the anchor's component... i.e., the stamp must not create new adjacent connections?? Actually maybe the rule requires the stamp's non-anchor cells land on bg, AND the anchor must be a SINGLE (isolated). And the diagonal motif stamp at 6@(9,) can't happen since anchor would collide with existing 4@(8,8).

So the fix: require the anchor cell to be an isolated single. Then re-derive which singles got stamped in demo5:
- 4@(0,2)→6 left ✓ isolated? yes single comp.
- 4@(0,9)→6 left ✓
- 4@(1,1)→6 above ✓ (from shape (7,8)6-V (8,8)4 V? no that's diag (7,8),(8,8)? earlier I wrote (7,8),(8,8) as vertical 6-over-4).
- 4@(1,8)→6 above ✓
- 4@(2,22)→6 above ✓
- 6@(1,11)→4 right ✓
- 6@(3,12)→4 up-left ✓ (offset (-1,-1) from shape ((8,8,4),(9,9,6))? that's 6 at (9,9), 4 at (8,8): anchor 6@(9,9)?? (9,9) is bg in input... wait input (9,9)=8. Hmm (3,12)=6 added, anchor 6@(9,9)? no.

Hmm, this is getting complicated; rather than debug manually, run the candidate solution function on all three demos. Given budget concerns, maybe just request more demos? Wrong attempts 0/8, demo requests 6/8. We still have 2 demo requests and 8 wrong attempts. The instruction says submit only when all demos match. Better to iterate in the REPL this turn: fix the solver, validate on all 6 demos, then submit test answer. But the turn budget stopped me mid-debug. I need efficient turns: keep tool calls compact, end reply with action line.

Let me write clean careful code this time.

    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=set(); out=[]
